Reusing the resolver fits better because it already owns this view's settings. Defaults are defined in `settings/resolver.ts:12`, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes the resolved values. I traced that path end to end. A new key there reaches the view through the same flow every existing setting uses.

A view-local settings object would put a second settings source beside the one that owns every other setting. Its defaults could drift from the resolver's. The view would read from two places. Anything that later reads or overrides settings through the resolver would not see this one. So the decision is the existing resolver, and I'll record it in the draft.

The open behavior question is what happens to active report filters when the user switches workspaces. That decides what the new setting controls and what its default is. Which behavior should the setting produce?

A) Clear filters on workspace switch by default, with the setting letting users keep them
B) Keep today's behavior by default (filters carry over), with the setting letting users opt into clearing
C) Remember filters separately for each workspace, with the setting turning that memory on or off
D) other - name it

Recommendation: A - the reported problem is that carried-over filters hide rows in the new workspace, so clearing by default fixes it for everyone. Users who rely on carry-over can still turn it back on.
